newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine foreign debt $8.84 bln at start '97-FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine foreign debt $8.84 bln at start '97-FinMin.

text.p: Ukraine's foreign debt grew to $8.84 billion on January 1 from $8.04 billion a year ago, with about half of the money owed to former Soviet republics, the deputy finance minister said on Tuesday.
Serhiy Makatsaria told parliament Ukraine owes $4.205 billion mostly to Russia and Turkmenistan, Ukraine's main gas suppliers.
"This is, in fact, money which state enterprises borrowed in earlier years, from 1991 to 1995, for gas and energy, which the government now must pay," he said.
The deputy minister said the government would this month devise a plan to pay off the $860 million owed by the 40 enterprises and whose loans it guaranteed.
"Today Ukraine is far from a critical point in terms of the volume of money it owes to foreign creditors," Makatsaria said.
He said Ukraine has borrowed $2.2 billion from the International Monetary Fund since 1994, using part of the money to build up central bank reserves.

Ukraine is expected to resume talks soon for receipt of a three-year, $2.5 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) from the IMF, which will decide whether to give Ukraine the money once the country passes the 1997 budget.
Parliamentary Speaker Olexander Moroz said debate to give the draft a second reading -- thus passing it -- could start this week if the government forwards the document to parliament.
Credits received since 1994 to finance the deficit have totalled $1.29 billion, including $900 million from the World Bank, $241 million from the EU, and $150 million from Japan.
European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) credits for projects totalled $228 million.
